## Williams看見通膨改善、聘僱不如預期，美債止跌

Williams質疑高油價必然導致聯準會再升息的判斷，ADP又公布較弱的民間聘僱，美債殖利率因而穩定。2年、10年及30年期分別維持4.39%、4.79%及5.27%，5年期下降1個基點至4.54%。WTI與布蘭特仍在$90.58及$95.18的高檔。

止跌並未逆轉市場已反映的緊縮。一週來2年期殖利率仍上升20個基點，10年期升13；2s10s維持40個基點，週內收窄7個基點。10年期實質殖利率又升1個基點至2.45%，由損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.34%抵銷。

S&P 500近350檔股票上漲，VIX收15.2，高收益利差變化不大。但褐皮書仍描述價格溫和加速，歐洲天然氣成本也持續壓抑當地債券。當日訊息讓投資人有理由不把美國升息視為必然，尚未證明高實質利率環境即將結束。

海外政策結果也說明這種差異。紐西蘭雖升息，指引卻讓下次行動可以再等，2年期殖利率反而下降；加拿大維持利率但強調通膨風險，使短端上升。信用市場方面，Kingspan完成發債並取得需求，Bathla貸款人對贖回及完工融資則採不同做法。Ukrenergo重整尤其需要分清：新借款有保證，交換給既有債權人的新券沒有。

## Williams主張耐心觀察，就業增長集中在少數產業

Williams接受CNBC訪問時表示，關稅效果正在消退，高能源價格未擴散至其他服務。他認為7月政策設定有利兼顧就業與通膨，仍須依後續證據評估。這不是承諾維持利率，而是反對只憑油價就決定升息。

他將部分殖利率上升連結至AI投資及較強成長預期，但表示尚無證據確認持久生產力繁榮足以提高中性利率，自己的估計仍約1%。在他的判斷裡，投資增加資金需求，與貨幣中性水準永久改變，是兩回事。

ADP公布8月民間就業增加3.8萬，低於預估4.7萬及7月4.6萬。教育醫療增4.5萬、休閒餐旅1.6萬、建築1.2萬、金融6,000；製造業減1.7萬、專業服務1.6萬，貿易運輸公用事業及天然資源採礦各減5,000，資訊減4,000。大型企業增加3.4萬職位，員工少於50人的公司僅增3,000。聘僱集中，薪資增長卻仍穩定。

週三公布、資料蒐集至8月24日的褐皮書，呈現略不同的情況：經濟溫和成長、就業小增，前景整體正面。國防與資料中心訂單支撐多數地區製造業，製造、建築及部分服務聘僱相對健康，零售與餐旅較弱。調查對象及期間不同，有助理解為何這份資料並未對應ADP的製造減員、餐旅增聘。

各區案例也顯示，專業人才需求可以與其他職位減少並存。里奇蒙提到資料中心積極搶人，一家馬里蘭建商為留任加薪35%；紐約企業難找熟練AI工程師，卻減少初階科技及行政人力需求；費城業者將後台自動化，職缺下降也使求職媒合等待名單更長。

多數地區價格溫和加速，消費者卻限制了轉嫁空間。克里夫蘭製造需求強，消費支出則連續第四期小幅下降；亞特蘭大零售商看到消費降級，餐廳每次消費金額減少；芝加哥更多信用卡用戶僅繳最低款，整體消費放款品質仍持平。舊金山則將生產力改善約各半歸因於AI，以及訓練、流程等其他變化。成本壓力明確存在，但尚未形成全面聘僱熱潮或中性利率確已提高的證據。

## 紐西蘭升息推升債券，加拿大維持利率卻使殖利率上行

紐西蘭央行連續第二次升息25個基點至2.75%，總裁Anna Breman卻強調後續時點不確定，須先評估已採取的行動。2年期公債殖利率下降7個基點至3.58%，匯率最多跌1%；10月升息機率由65%降至約36%，但12月前再升仍幾乎完全反映。

第4季平均政策利率預測由5月的2.84%降至2.81%，到2027年中為3.07%。第3季通膨預估卻從3.3%升至3.9%，回到2%中點的時間，也從2027年第3季延至2028年初。核心通膨2.7%、長期預期近2%，仍讓央行有時間觀察閒置產能及復甦。固定房貸利率多已上調，在以固定利率為主的市場，這次決策立即新增的影響較有限。

澳洲第2季GDP增0.4%，優於0.3%預估；年增2.1%，也高於市場1.8%及央行1.9%預測。3年期殖利率最多升11個基點至4.83%；交換市場完全反映11月升息，2027年第1季再升機率由62%升至約80%。消費與民間需求支撐結果，但大型資料中心投資、颶風後礦業出口恢復，以及家庭因油價而調整的行為，使成長廣度仍須審慎看待。稍後紐西蘭指引協助澳債收斂跌幅。

加拿大如預期連續第七次維持2.25%，Macklem卻強調通膨上行風險增加。2年期殖利率突破3.09%，為3月以來盤中最高，加幣也升值。他認為能源比新一輪美國關稅更值得擔心，並指出高額關稅涵蓋約5%對美出口；受影響企業傷害嚴重，不一定代表整體經濟持續受到大幅拖累。整體通膨3%，核心壓力約2%。

植田要求在底層通膨接近2%時更加注意上行風險，也未反對市場完全反映9月升息。高田更進一步表示，25個基點並非固定步幅，連續升息也可能；但未承諾50或75個基點。7月多數維持近1%時，他曾獨自主張1.25%，因此這是既有鷹派的談話，不是委員會已同意的計畫。

日圓在談話後、紐約時段加速，最多升1.2%至每美元158.22，之後回吐部分漲幅。交易員猜測有官方詢價或干預，但兩者皆未明確獲證實。日圓強勢協助美元下降、黃金上升，不等於確認又一次官方操作完成。

日本企業已因國內利率提高而改變決策。彭博8月向30家非金融企業發出調查，取得14家回覆；這30家企業共有¥6.74兆債券將在9月1日至2028年8月31日到期。Toyota與東北電力表示，未來兩年日圓債再融資可能使年度利息支出增加逾30%。KDDI考慮出售資產減債，中國電力可能加速處分資產與策略持股，大和房屋則檢視房產投資報酬門檻。

東京電力電網已提前籌資或正在考慮提前，JERA則提到外幣借款、利率交換及擴大投資人基礎。今年日本企業發行的美元及歐元債，合計已逾$1,100億；透過交換換回日圓，有時可取得與本地發債相近、甚至更低的成本。

丹麥8月淨買入DKK56億，6月曾買入DKK7億；政策利率1.85%，比歐洲央行低40個基點。干預提高丹麥可能獨立升息支撐匯率盯住的討論，但分析師認為並非近期事件，通常還需更大累計買入才有必要。

## 天然氣與燃料短缺壓縮財政空間

歐洲天然氣上漲約3%至每兆瓦時€74以上，創今年高點。英國10年期殖利率盤中達5.29%後回落，德國升至3.39%；Stoxx Europe 600跌0.2%，對照美股回升。儲氣率僅65%，為2009年有紀錄以來同期最低。

烏克蘭攻擊煉油廠、波斯灣出貨減少及煉油運作受損，壓縮成品油供應。AAA資料顯示美國汽油每加侖逾$4、柴油接近$6。週三美軍攻擊伊朗雷達及布雷能力，伊朗則宣稱報復區域內美軍基地。即使原油單日未再大漲，這些瓶頸仍增加家庭與企業成本。

英國首相Andy Burnham在國會答詢時承諾遵守財政規則，但未排除借款或加稅。規則要求2029年日常支出由收入支應；Bloomberg Economics估計，殖利率及通膨提高，已耗去原有£236億緩衝中的約£120億。Burnham尚未說明將如何調整稅收或支出，以保住剩餘空間。

Nagel表示，取消歐元體系央行持有的國家債務，會構成禁止的貨幣融通，回應的是Mélenchon提案的原則，不是已達成的債權處理。法國10年期對德債利差上午接近但未達88個基點。他支持市場對9月歐洲央行升息的預期，卻因能源波動及可能擴散的影響，對之後仍謹慎。

負責Lula政綱的José Sérgio Gabrielli反對停止實質最低工資增加，或削弱強制醫療教育支出規則，偏好提高補貼與配置效率，也質疑3%通膨目標的僵硬程度。財長Dario Durigan承認投資人擔心債務有道理；Gabrielli談話不是總統最後決定。總債務已達GDP 82.5%，2023年以來增逾10個百分點。逾$3,000億儲備、可支應近八個月到期債的國庫緩衝，提供流動性，不是已敲定的支出調整。

美國能源部長Chris Wright表示，中國對委內瑞拉新增石油收入沒有債務請求權，重整工作正在進行。這是政府立場，不是法院確認的清償方案。Chevron規畫五年投資$70億，Wright稱GE Vernova及Eni協議已簽署；並將用原油交換補充美國戰略儲備，而非直接存入重油。長期承諾仍無法替代目前受航運及煉油限制的燃料。

## 新券找到買方，基金結構呈現不同流動性風險

Kingspan以兩檔綠色債募集€8.5億，最終訂單€31億，低於高峰逾€46億；對交換利率利差為63及95個基點，預期標普與惠譽均評BBB，用途為合格專案。資料中心材料訂單支持較佳獲利展望。最終訂單證明有需求，不能把高峰簿記全視為定價後仍留下的資金。

Waymo首次借款正進入最後洽談，金額逾$30億，貸款方包括Pimco、Blackstone及Sixth Street，高盛顧問。未評級債務可能高於基準加500個基點，條件尚未定。公司在美國14城每週提供逾50萬趟付費服務，但車隊與AI擴張需要傳統股本以外的資金。先前以$1,260億估值募集$160億股本，不代表這筆債務獲得保證。

Uber另宣布裁員約3,300人、占全球10%，減少管理層級並將資源轉向叫車、外送及自駕計程車。科技融資與聘僱並非一致增長。收購貸款方面，銀行正為Apax收購Gerresheimer的Primary Packaging Plastics及Centor，安排約€10億定期貸款及循環額度；收購宣布時估值€15億，聯貸分銷與定價仍開放。

歐洲央行研究人員發現，合成風險移轉發行增加1%，與股利增加0.07%相關，企業貸款卻只增加0.02%，經濟效果相當小。資本釋放與分散不會自動帶來大量新企業信用，交易對手及到期續作風險也仍重要。

Mark Walter旗下兩大保險公司6月底欠印第安納波利斯聯邦住房貸款銀行逾$60億，比半年前多36%，約為2025年初兩倍。他控制的保險公司另借出逾$200億給關係企業。這兩種不同曝險顯示融資依賴與關係人集中，卻不能直接把某筆FHLB借款追溯成某筆關係人貸款。

Bathla債權人採取不同流動性做法。Centuria Bass雖預期基金不會受重大影響，仍暫停兩檔工具贖回；曝險逾A$3億的PAG因認為擔保及回收順位較佳，維持提款，並承諾直接付款給312戶開發案承包商。Balmain則規畫再提供A$100萬，完成Kembla Grange另一棟建物。

一名債權人將土地、房產及房貸付款擔保品估值逾A$45億，但回收仍取決於順位、工程階段及完工成本，不只是總值。MSCI Research指出，澳洲約A$2,000億私人信用市場，房地產占比可達60%，北美僅15%至20%。贖回條件與支應完工能力不同，同一家開發商出事，也可能對各貸款人造成不同影響。

## 流動性支持不等於困境債回收已定

中國中央及地方前八個月使用年度發債額度約68%，低於一年前76%；國債單獨為65%，2022年以來最慢。要求加快預算執行之際，人民銀行中期借貸與買斷式逆回購，8月由7月CN¥8,000億降至CN¥1,000億，未來發債加速仍有增加支持空間。

亞洲時段美中10年期利差達312個基點，接近約315紀錄，中債殖利率約1.69%，人民幣卻維持每美元約6.72。資本管制、企業換匯及7月底外資僅占公債市場4.6%，限制了利差擴大必然導致外流的推論，儲備分散及熊貓債發行仍可吸引資金。

印度吸引$1,360億外幣、主要為僑民存款，超過央行估計$800億。但國內非銀行機構仍在成本上升與季節需求下，規畫至少₹1,000億債券：Power Finance至多₹500億、Bajaj Housing至多₹200億、HDB Financial至少₹100億、Tata Capital至少₹150億、Shriram逾₹50億。這些是擬議交易，不是已完成發行，也不代表本地成本下降。

Vingroup討論首次3年韓元私募，至多約₩4,000億、$2.92億作一般用途，董事會原授權至多₩4,550億；目前規模及條件仍初步。Shinhan Securities Vietnam、KB Securities及Kiwoom參與，提供可能的新買方來源，尚未確定最後借款成本。

土耳其考慮課徵機構貨幣市場基金報酬稅，該類資產約TRY3兆、$620億，但只是估計$750億外資套利的一部分：其中約$100億在里拉貨幣基金，$650億在遠期外匯。高盛估計8月較快貶值使單月套利報酬低於1%，央行融資則從40%回到主要37%利率。支持里拉儲蓄及儲備的誘因也有助通膨下降，突然撤回會有代價；稅制仍是提案。秘魯同樣尚未通過Keiko Fujimori提交國會、取消法定貸款利率上限的法案。

Ukrenergo取得美國DFC對至少$4.45億新債的支持，由花旗安排，用來買回已違約債券。保證涵蓋這筆融資，不涵蓋換給既有持有人的證券。$8.25億2028年境外債持有人可選面額60%至65.125%的現金，或一比一交換成未保證的8.5%新債；交換券自2028年6月起分八期平均攤還，交割不久支付自2025年7月起的利息。現金部分上限$4.45億，須成功發行DFC支持債券，也須取得債權人同意。

交易員將塞內加爾反彈歸因於空頭回補，而非債務處理公告後信心改善，Van Eck趁需求減碼。投資人仍爭論2028年歐元債待遇，牽涉3月$5.47億本息付款。部分人期待短券有較佳選項，摩根士丹利則警告，如果擴大納入重整的債權範圍不如期待，長券仍有下檔。價格反彈尚未逆轉重整風險。

## 服務業、非農與日本長債標售是眼前考驗

9月3日紐約時間上午8:30公布初領，預期20.5萬、前值20.3萬；10點ISM服務業估54.3、前值54.1。9月4日8:30非農預估增5.8萬，前期減2.3萬，失業率4.1%，平均時薪月增率由0.1%加速至0.3%。服務價格、薪資及聘僱廣度，比小幅超預期的總數更能檢驗Williams等待的理由。

日本9月3日30年期標售，殖利率約4.155%，壽險買入加快，前兩次約4%標售也有相對強勁投標倍數。高田擴大可能政策步幅的說法，使進場價位更難判斷。需求將顯示國內買方能否承接新增不確定性，或需要更高殖利率、進而吸引海外債券資金回流。

塞內加爾9月13日息票決定將用實際付款政策檢驗反彈。Ukrenergo 10月1日債權人會議及DFC支持募資，則決定擬議現金與交換選項能否生效。即使基準殖利率穩定，兩者仍各有執行條件。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasuries pause as Williams sees inflation progress and hiring disappoints

Treasury yields steadied as John Williams challenged the presumption that high oil prices must lead to another Fed increase, while ADP reported weaker-than-expected private hiring. Two-, 10- and 30-year yields held at 4.39%, 4.79% and 5.27%; the 5-year fell 1 basis point to 4.54%. WTI and Brent remained elevated at $90.58 and $95.18.

The pause did not reverse the tightening already reflected in markets. Two-year yields were still 20 basis points higher over the week, compared with 13 at ten years. The 2s10s spread remained 40 basis points after narrowing 7 over that period. Ten-year real yields rose another basis point to 2.45%, offset by a 1-basis-point breakeven decline to 2.34%.

Nearly 350 S&P 500 stocks advanced, VIX closed at 15.2 and high-yield spreads were little changed. Yet the Beige Book described moderately accelerating prices, and European gas costs kept regional bonds under pressure. The day gave investors reasons not to assume an automatic US hike, without establishing that the higher real-rate environment was ending.

Policy outcomes abroad underscored that distinction. New Zealand raised rates but its 2-year yield fell as guidance allowed more time before the next move. Canada held but emphasized inflation risk, sending short yields higher. In credit, completed Kingspan issuance attracted demand, while Bathla lenders took different approaches to withdrawals and completion funding. Ukrenergo's proposed restructuring made a particularly important distinction between guaranteed new borrowing and unguaranteed exchange notes.

## Williams offers patience; ADP and the Beige Book show uneven labor demand

Williams told CNBC that tariff effects were fading and expensive energy was not spreading into other services. He regarded July's policy setting as well placed to balance employment and inflation, subject to incoming evidence. That was not a commitment to hold; it disputed the idea that oil alone settled the case for an increase.

He linked part of the rise in yields to AI investment and stronger growth expectations, but said evidence did not yet establish a lasting productivity boom sufficient to raise the neutral rate. His estimate remained around 1%. Investment demand for capital and a durable change in monetary neutrality were separate questions in his assessment.

ADP reported 38,000 private jobs in August, below the 47,000 forecast and July's 46,000. Education and health added 45,000, leisure and hospitality 16,000, construction 12,000 and finance 6,000. Manufacturing lost 17,000, professional services 16,000, trade/transport/utilities and natural resources/mining each 5,000, and information 4,000. Large firms added 34,000 jobs; those with fewer than 50 employees added just 3,000. Pay growth stayed stable despite the narrow base of hiring.

The Beige Book, published Wednesday with information through August 24, gave a somewhat different picture: modest growth, slightly higher employment and a positive outlook. Defense and data-center orders supported manufacturing across most districts, with relatively healthy hiring in manufacturing, construction and some services; retail and hospitality were weaker. Different populations and collection periods helped explain why its sector picture did not match ADP's manufacturing losses and hospitality gains.

The district anecdotes showed how specialized demand could coexist with fewer opportunities elsewhere. Richmond cited aggressive data-center competition for workers, including a Maryland builder's 35% retention pay increase. New York contacts struggled to find skilled AI engineers while reducing demand for entry-level technology and administrative staff. Philadelphia firms automated back offices and reported longer placement waitlists as openings declined.

Prices accelerated moderately in most districts, but consumers constrained pass-through. Cleveland combined robust manufacturing with a fourth consecutive period of modest spending declines. Atlanta retailers reported trading down and restaurants lower spending per visit. Chicago saw more credit-card users making minimum payments, although overall consumer-loan quality was flat. San Francisco attributed productivity improvements roughly equally to AI and to training, processes and other changes. The reports left identifiable cost pressures without demonstrating a uniform hiring boom or a clearly higher neutral rate.

## New Zealand's hike lifts bonds; Canada's hold sends yields higher

The RBNZ raised its cash rate 25 basis points to 2.75%, a second consecutive hike, while Anna Breman stressed uncertainty about further timing and the need to assess moves already made. Two-year government yields fell 7 basis points to 3.58%, and the currency declined as much as 1%. October hike odds dropped to about 36% from 65%, though a move by December remained almost fully priced.

The projected Q4 average cash rate slipped to 2.81% from May's 2.84%, reaching 3.07% by mid-2027. Q3 inflation was raised to 3.9% from 3.3%, and the return to the 2% midpoint delayed to early 2028 from Q3 2027. Core inflation of 2.7% and longer-term expectations near 2% nevertheless allowed time to assess spare capacity and recovery. Many fixed mortgage rates had already increased, limiting the immediate extra effect on a predominantly fixed-rate market.

Australia's Q2 GDP rose 0.4%, above a 0.3% forecast, with annual growth of 2.1% exceeding the 1.8% consensus and RBA's 1.9% projection. Three-year yields rose as much as 11 basis points to 4.83%. Swaps fully priced a November hike and put another Q1 2027 increase at about 80%, up from 62%. Consumption and private demand supported the result, though lumpy data-center investment, post-cyclone mining exports and fuel-related household behavior qualified its breadth. New Zealand's guidance later helped trim Australian losses.

Canada held at 2.25% for a seventh meeting, as expected, but Tiff Macklem emphasized greater upside inflation risk. Two-year yields exceeded 3.09%, their highest intraday since March, and the currency strengthened. He regarded energy as the bigger concern after renewed US tariffs, noting that the steep duties covered about 5% of Canadian exports to the US. The affected businesses faced serious damage without necessarily creating a large persistent aggregate drag. Headline inflation was 3%, with core pressure around 2%.

Ueda called for greater attention to upside prices as underlying inflation approached 2%, without resisting fully priced September hike expectations. Takata went further: 25-basis-point steps were not fixed and consecutive moves remained possible. He did not promise 50 or 75 basis points. His July dissent for 1.25%, against a majority holding near 1%, identified the remarks as those of an established hawk rather than the board's agreed plan.

The yen accelerated during New York trading after the comments, gaining as much as 1.2% to 158.22 before retracing some of it. Traders speculated about official rate checks or intervention, but neither was clearly confirmed. Yen strength helped lower the dollar and lift gold without establishing another completed official operation.

Higher domestic rates were already changing Japanese corporate decisions. Fourteen of 30 nonfinancial companies answered Bloomberg's August survey; the full contacted group had ¥6.74 trillion of bonds maturing from September 1 through August 31, 2028. Toyota and Tohoku Electric said refinancing next-two-year yen maturities could raise annual interest expense more than 30%. KDDI considered asset sales to reduce debt, Chugoku Electric saw faster disposals of assets and strategic shares, and Daiwa House reviewed property hurdle rates.

TEPCO Power Grid had advanced funding or was considering doing so. JERA cited foreign-currency borrowing, swaps and a wider buyer base. Japanese issuers sold over $110 billion in dollar and euro notes this year, with swaps sometimes producing comparable or lower yen-equivalent costs. Those are funding choices beyond a simple shift from foreign to domestic bonds.

Denmark bought a net 5.6 billion kroner in August after 0.7 billion in June. Its 1.85% policy rate was 40 basis points below the ECB's. Intervention raised the possibility of an independent Danish increase to support the peg, although analysts saw no imminent move and expected much greater cumulative purchases before one became necessary.

## Gas and fuel shortages tighten the fiscal room

European gas rose about 3% above €74 per megawatt-hour, a year-to-date high. Ten-year gilt yields reached 5.29% intraday before paring gains; Bund yields rose to 3.39%. The Stoxx Europe 600 fell 0.2% while US stocks recovered. Gas inventories were only 65% full, the lowest seasonal level in records back to 2009.

Ukrainian refinery attacks, fewer Persian Gulf cargoes and impaired refining tightened finished-fuel supply. US gasoline exceeded $4 a gallon and diesel approached $6, according to AAA. Wednesday's US strikes targeted Iranian radar and mine-laying capabilities; Iran reported retaliation against US regional bases. Even without another large daily crude jump, these bottlenecks continued to raise household and business costs.

At prime minister's questions, Andy Burnham pledged to follow UK fiscal rules but declined to exclude either borrowing or tax rises. Bloomberg Economics estimated higher yields and inflation had removed about £12 billion of the £23.6 billion buffer against balancing day-to-day spending with revenue in 2029. The commitment did not specify the tax or spending choices needed to preserve that room.

Nagel said canceling national debt held by Eurosystem central banks would be prohibited monetary financing, addressing the principle behind Mélenchon's proposal rather than an agreed creditor treatment. France's 10-year spread traded just below 88 basis points over Bunds during the morning. He also endorsed expectations of a September ECB increase while remaining cautious beyond it given energy volatility and possible wider effects.

Brazil's José Sérgio Gabrielli, coordinating Lula's platform, rejected ending real minimum-wage increases or weakening mandatory health and education spending rules. He preferred more efficient subsidies and allocations and questioned the rigidity of the 3% inflation target. Finance Minister Dario Durigan acknowledged legitimate investor debt concerns; Gabrielli's remarks were not a final presidential decision. Gross debt had reached 82.5% of GDP, up more than 10 percentage points since 2023. Reserves above $300 billion and a Treasury buffer for almost eight months of maturities offered liquidity, not a settled spending adjustment.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said China would have no debt claim on revenue from new Venezuelan oil production and that restructuring work was under way. That was the administration's position, not an adjudicated settlement. Chevron planned $7 billion of investment over five years; Wright said GE Vernova and Eni agreements were signed. He described crude swaps to replenish US emergency reserves rather than directly storing the heavy oil. These longer-term commitments did not replace the fuel currently constrained by shipping and refining.

## New issuance finds buyers while fund structures expose different liquidity risks

Kingspan raised €850 million in two green tranches with final orders of €3.1 billion, down from a peak above €4.6 billion. Spreads were 63 and 95 basis points over mid-swaps; both tranches were expected BBB at S&P and Fitch, with proceeds for eligible projects. Data-center materials orders supported an improved profit outlook. Final orders demonstrated demand without treating the larger peak book as money remaining at the agreed price.

Waymo was in final talks for over $3 billion of debut borrowing from lenders including Pimco, Blackstone and Sixth Street, advised by Goldman Sachs. The unrated debt could cost more than 500 basis points over its benchmark; terms were not final. The business served over 500,000 paid weekly rides in 14 US cities but needed capital for fleet and AI expansion beyond its traditional equity base. Its earlier $16 billion equity raise at a $126 billion valuation did not guarantee the debt.

Uber separately announced about 3,300 job cuts, 10% of global staff, reducing management layers while directing resources to ride-sharing, delivery and robotaxis. Technology financing and employment growth were not moving uniformly together. In acquisition lending, banks were assembling about €1 billion of term loans and revolvers for Apax's purchase of Primary Packaging Plastics and Centor from Gerresheimer, valued at €1.5 billion when announced. Syndication and pricing remained open.

ECB researchers found that a 1% increase in synthetic risk-transfer issuance was associated with 0.07% more dividends but only 0.02% more corporate lending, an economically small lending effect in their assessment. Capital relief and diversification did not automatically produce substantial new business credit, and counterparty and rollover risks remained relevant.

Mark Walter's two largest insurers owed more than $6 billion to FHLB Indianapolis at end-June, 36% more than six months earlier and about twice the start-2025 level. Insurers he controls also lent over $20 billion to affiliated businesses. Those distinct exposures highlight funding dependence and related-party concentration; they do not trace individual FHLB advances into specific affiliate loans.

Bathla creditors showed different liquidity responses. Centuria Bass suspended redemptions in two vehicles despite expecting no material fund impact. PAG, with over A$300 million exposed, kept withdrawals open because it considered its security and recovery position stronger, and committed to paying contractors directly on a 312-apartment project. Balmain planned another A$1 million to complete a Kembla Grange building.

One creditor valued land, properties and mortgage-payment collateral above A$4.5 billion. Recovery still depends on priority, construction stage and the cost of completion, not just aggregate collateral. Australia's roughly A$200 billion private-credit market has as much as 60% in property, versus 15%–20% in North America according to MSCI Research. Different redemption terms and the ability to fund work through completion can spread the consequences unevenly across lenders to the same developer.

## Liquidity support does not settle distressed recoveries

China's central and local authorities had used about 68% of annual bond quotas in eight months, versus 76% a year earlier. Sovereign issuance alone was 65%, its slowest pace since 2022. Calls for faster budget implementation came as PBOC medium-term lending and outright reverse repos fell to 100 billion yuan in August from 800 billion in July, leaving room for more support as sales accelerate.

The US-China 10-year gap reached 312 basis points in Asian trading, near the roughly 315 record, with Chinese yields around 1.69%. The yuan nevertheless held near 6.72 per dollar. Capital controls, corporate conversions and foreign ownership of only 4.6% of the government-bond market at end-July limited a mechanical yield-gap outflow. Reserve diversification and panda issuance could still attract funds.

India attracted $136 billion of foreign currency, mostly diaspora deposits, above the RBI's $80 billion estimate. Domestic nonbanks nonetheless planned at least 100 billion rupees of bonds amid rising costs and seasonal demand: Power Finance up to 50 billion, Bajaj Housing up to 20 billion, HDB Financial at least 10 billion, Tata Capital at least 15 billion and Shriram more than 5 billion. These were proposed deals, not completed placements or evidence of falling local costs.

Vingroup discussed a debut three-year won private placement up to about 400 billion won, or $292 million, for general purposes. Its board had authorized up to 455 billion; current size and terms remained preliminary. Shinhan Securities Vietnam, KB Securities and Kiwoom worked on the deal, adding a potential investor pool without yet establishing the final borrowing cost.

Turkey considered taxing institutional money-market fund returns. That segment held about 3 trillion liras, or $62 billion, but was only one part of estimated $75 billion foreign carry positions: roughly $10 billion in lira money-market funds and $65 billion in forwards. Faster August depreciation reduced monthly carry returns below 1%, according to Goldman Sachs, while central-bank funding reverted from 40% to the main 37% rate. Incentives supporting lira savings and reserves also mattered for disinflation, making an abrupt withdrawal costly. The tax was still a proposal. Peru likewise had not enacted Keiko Fujimori's proposed removal of the statutory loan-rate ceiling, included in bills before Congress.

Ukrenergo secured US DFC backing for at least $445 million of new bonds arranged with Citigroup to fund repurchases of defaulted notes. The guarantee covers that financing, not the securities offered in exchange to existing holders. Owners of the $825 million 2028 Eurobond could take cash at 60%–65.125% of face or exchange one-for-one into unguaranteed 8.5% debt. Exchange notes amortize in eight equal installments from June 2028 and pay interest shortly after settlement for the period from July 2025. The cash leg is capped at $445 million and needs successful DFC-backed issuance; creditor consent is also required.

Senegal's rebound was attributed by traders to short covering, not improved confidence after the debt-treatment announcement. Van Eck used demand to reduce exposure. Investors continued to debate the 2028 euro bond's treatment, with a $547 million March principal-and-interest payment at stake. Some hoped for better options for short-dated holders; Morgan Stanley warned of longer-bond downside if expectations of a broader creditor perimeter proved wrong. The bounce did not establish a reversal of restructuring risk.

## Services, payrolls and Japan's long auction are the immediate tests

Initial claims arrive September 3 at 8:30 a.m. New York time, with 205,000 expected after 203,000. ISM services follows at 10 a.m., forecast at 54.3 versus 54.1. September 4 payrolls at 8:30 a.m. are expected to rise 58,000 after a 23,000 decline, with unemployment at 4.1% and monthly hourly earnings accelerating to 0.3% from 0.1%. Service prices, wages and the breadth of hiring will test Williams's case for patience more directly than a small headline beat.

Japan's September 3 30-year auction comes with yields around 4.155%, accelerating insurer purchases and relatively strong coverage at the prior two sales around 4%. Takata's wider range of possible policy moves complicates the entry point. Demand will show whether domestic buyers can absorb the additional uncertainty or require still higher yields, potentially drawing capital from overseas bonds.

Senegal's September 13 coupon decision will test its rebound against payment policy. Ukrenergo's October 1 creditor meeting and DFC-backed fundraising determine whether proposed cash and exchange choices become effective. Both remain execution questions even if benchmark yields stabilize.
